bullets.title: Apple hits $5T market cap; launches hardware leasing via Klarna
bullets.body: Apple briefly crossed a $5 trillion market cap today, becoming only the second company ever to do so (after Nvidia). Simultaneously, Apple launched its 'Apple Upgrade' leasing program via Klarna: iPhones from $17.99/month, MacBook Air from $24.99/month, with an all-in bundle (iPhone 17 + MacBook Air + Watch) for ~$61/month. One analyst noted this removes the need for price cuts while expanding ecosystem access, making competing PC ecosystems 'less competitive on value.'

bullets.title: NVDA: Moonshot seeks more Blackwell chips; Huang meets Lutnick; Taipei office raided
bullets.body: Multiple NVDA signals in the window: Chinese AI startup Moonshot is actively sourcing additional Nvidia Blackwell GPUs for its Kimi K4 model, sustaining enterprise demand. CEO Jensen Huang met with Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick amid ongoing China export scrutiny. Separately, Taiwan authorities raided Nvidia's Taipei office as part of an AI chip-smuggling dragnet, resulting in arrests.

bullets.title: Nvidia at $4.8T market cap; analyst touts 2.5%-accurate 2.6-year-old revenue forecast
bullets.body: One fintwit analyst highlighted that his Nvidia revenue forecast from 2.6 years ago was off by only 2.5% (~$2B), with Q1 2026 revenue forecasted at $79.6B. NVDA and AAPL were also cited as having the most bullish options flow on the day. A separate note put NVDA's market cap at ~$4.8T, with Huang's personal stake worth ~$160B.

bullets.title: Semis in historic drawdown: SOXX -25.7%, Goldman momentum basket worst month on record
bullets.body: The SOXX ETF is in a 25.7% drawdown from highs. Goldman's high-beta momentum basket is on track for its worst monthly performance in history, worse than 2000 and 2009. Top H1 Russell 1K winners are down 36% on average in June/July; SNDK alone is down 51% this month after leading the index in H1. JPM's TMT specialist cited weak earnings reactions, 'circular financing concerns,' and anxiety over CSPs cutting capex as drivers.

bullets.title: DELL plunges 14.8% — largest single-day decline since April — on AI selloff
bullets.body: Dell Technologies fell 14.8% in its largest single-day decline since April 2025, swept up in the broader AI infrastructure selloff. The Nasdaq 100 entered a technical correction (down >10% from its ATH) while equal-weighted S&P 500 outperformed significantly, up 2%+ on the week vs QQQ -5%+.

bullets.title: AMD down 10% intraday; CEO Lisa Su flags AI inflection point
bullets.body: AMD fell 10% during the session as part of the broader semiconductor selloff. CEO Lisa Su separately commented that 'AI is at an inflection point where more and more people are doing useful work.' An analyst noted AMD management discussed potential neocloud expansion with 152 MW available for lease, already entrenched with HotAisle and Tensorwave.

bullets.title: MU: Analyst projects $254B NTM revenue, 44% of $920B market cap in 8 quarters
bullets.body: A bullish analyst estimated Micron will generate $254B in revenue over the next 4 quarters and another $310B in the following 4, representing 44% of its current ~$920B market cap at $810/share. The same analyst noted excessive leverage—not fundamentals—is driving the current selloff, and expects a strong rally once deleveraging completes. Large put positions were also noted being accumulated on MU by institutional players.

bullets.title: Celestica Q2 confirms AI infrastructure cycle broadening beyond single accelerator generation
bullets.body: Read-throughs from Celestica's Q2 2026 earnings call signal the AI infrastructure cycle is 'broadening, accelerating, and extending' beyond any single accelerator or networking generation. Separately, consigned AI racks will improve cash efficiency and margin quality at CLS but create revenue comparison distortions.

bullets.title: Corning Q2 read-through positive for AI demand; GLW guidance in-line at high end
bullets.body: Corning's Q2 2026 results provide a 'materially positive read-through for current AI infrastructure demand' but give a 'more nuanced signal on timing of optical scale-up and co-packaged photonics.' Q3 guidance: core EPS 85-89c vs. 86c consensus, core sales $4.9-5.0B vs. $5.0B estimate.

bullets.title: Photonics: Large long-term TAM but material near-term estimate risk across AVGO, MRVL, COHR, LITE, FN
bullets.body: A sector analyst flagged that photonics represents a very large long-term TAM but carries 'material near-term estimate risk' across AVGO, MRVL, COHR, LITE, and FN. InP (indium phosphide) is emerging as a supply chain chokepoint per Lumentum's CEO, with implications for lasers, optical engines, and AI infrastructure. The physical buildout is described as 'far from over' despite recent sentiment deterioration.

bullets.title: META and BlackRock partner on $14B El Paso data center
bullets.body: Meta and BlackRock announced a joint $14 billion partnership to develop and operate a data center in El Paso, Texas, focused on AI infrastructure expansion. This represents one of the largest single-site AI infrastructure investments announced.

bullets.title: AMZN: AI shopping assistant use doubled in 2025; UBS/Mizuho cut price targets
bullets.body: Amazon reported its AI shopping assistant usage more than doubled in 2025, with 50%+ of shoppers now open to AI handling the entire buying process. On the negative side, UBS cut AMZN's price target to $305 (from $333) and Mizuho trimmed to $320 (from $325), while BMO raised to $360 (from $355).

bullets.title: Brent crude plunges >5% below $84 on US-Iran deal optimism; Hormuz physical flows at zero
bullets.body: Brent crude fell more than 5% to below $84/barrel (WTI briefly under $80) as mediators reported the US and Iran are 'close to resurrecting' a failed MoU deal. Paradoxically, physical tanker flows through the Strait of Hormuz have reportedly stopped entirely, with algo-driven trading cited as the dominant price force. S&P futures hit HOD on the Iran deal rumor.

bullets.title: Nasdaq 100 enters correction; SPY gamma bearish; momentum stocks red for the year
bullets.body: The Nasdaq 100 fell 1.6% Tuesday and entered a technical correction (>10% from ATH). SPY gamma distribution remains bearish with $1B+ notional accumulating in lower strikes. Momentum stocks have turned red for the year. The equal-weighted S&P has significantly outperformed since early June as rotation accelerates beneath the surface.

bullets.title: Fed watch: FOMC meeting underway; rate hike odds at 29-40%; BofA says hold
bullets.body: The FOMC meeting began Tuesday at 10am; Chairman Warsh holds press conference Wednesday at 2:30pm ET. BofA says a July hike would be 'unprecedented'—the Fed has never hiked with less than 60% market odds priced in. Markets pricing 29-40% probability of a hike. Citadel Securities made a case for hiking. 30-year TIPS real yield hit an all-time high.

bullets.title: US consumer confidence misses; ADP hiring slows 5th straight week
bullets.body: US Conference Board Consumer Confidence came in at 90.8 for July vs. 92.4 estimate and 91.2 prior—the weakest 'Present Situation' reading in 5+ years. ADP weekly private hiring slowed for the fifth consecutive week to 15,000 jobs/week (vs. 35,750 in early May), compounding macro softness ahead of the FOMC.

bullets.title: China enters mass production of domestic immersion DUV lithography tools
bullets.body: Multiple sources confirm China has begun mass-producing domestic immersion DUV (deep ultraviolet) lithography tools, with SMIC, CXMT, YMTC, and HH among first recipients. SMEE has reportedly been shipping DUV immersion tools since May 2025. BofA separately argued ASML's market position in China is not under immediate threat, as replacing ASML's technology remains difficult.

bullets.title: INTC Foundry completes DoD RAMP-C program; unusual $8.8M OTM call printed
bullets.body: Intel Foundry completed the RAMP-C program—a Department of Defense initiative launched October 2021 to develop secure, leading-edge domestic semiconductor manufacturing. Separately, an unusual $8.8M out-of-the-money call option print on INTC was flagged, suggesting directional bullish positioning by a large trader.

bullets.title: Musk: Grok 4.6 (1.5T) launches Aug 7; Grok 4.7 (2.1T) follows weeks later
bullets.body: Elon Musk announced Grok 4.6 will release around August 7 as a 1.5T model with 'significantly improved SFT & RL,' followed by Grok 4.7 as a 2.1T model weeks later. Grok 4.7 is described as superior to 4.6 in most aspects except slightly slower serving speed.

bullets.title: AI sector credit stress: hyperscaler default insurance hits record; JPM flags capex cut anxiety
bullets.body: The cost of insuring against default by AI hyperscalers hit record levels intraday. JPM's TMT specialist highlighted 'circular financing concerns' and anxiety over content service providers cutting capex as key drivers of the semiconductor sector waterfall. One analyst warned the AI-driven corporate credit impulse 'is approaching a wall' and may require central bank intervention within 2-3 weeks.
